names.botanical: Triticum aestivum (Bread wheat) / Triticum durum (Durum wheat)

cultivation_relevance: Second most crucial food grain in India. In Gujarat, Bhal tract Durum wheat (Bhalia) is celebrated for its natural sweetness and GI-tag status.

climate_and_soil.climate_type: Temperate to subtropical cool dry winter climate
climate_and_soil.temperature_range_celsius: 10°C to 15°C during germination/tillering; 20°C to 25°C during ripening
climate_and_soil.annual_rainfall_mm: Needs 4 to 6 irrigations; rainfed Bhalia wheat thrives on conserved monsoon residual moisture
soil_types: Black cotton soil with high moisture retention
climate_and_soil.drainage: Well drained; stagnant water during seedling stage causes yellowing and stunted tillers

planting_details.sowing_time: Timely sown: November 1 to 20; Late sown: Up to December 10
planting_details.seed_rate: 40 kg/acre (100 kg/ha) for timely sown; 50 kg/acre (125 kg/ha) for late sown or Bhalia durum wheat

critical_stages: Crown Root Initiation (CRI at 20-25 DAS - Most Critical!)

nutrient_management.fym_manure_per_acre: 4 tonnes FYM applied 3 weeks before sowing
nutrient_management.recommended_npk_ratio: 48:24:16 kg/acre N:P2O5:K2O (Half N + full P & K as basal; remaining half N top-dressed at CRI first irrigation)
micronutrients: Zinc Sulphate 21% @ 10 kg/acre basal in zinc-deficient fields

harvest_and_yield.maturity_days: 115 - 135 days depending on variety and temperature
harvest_and_yield.harvesting_signs: Leaves and spikes turn golden yellow; grain is firm with <14% moisture
harvest_and_yield.expected_yield_per_acre: 18 to 24 Quintals per acre under irrigated conditions; 6 to 10 Quintals for rainfed Bhalia
harvest_and_yield.post_harvest_storage: Sun dry grain to 10-12% moisture; store in metallic bins with neem leaves to prevent storage weevils
